Both of you have built coherent cases, but you're each overreaching in ways that the A-share structure specifically punishes, and I want to name those before I lay out what I think the right posture actually is.

Aggressive, your asymmetry math is the weakest link and you know it. You keep quoting "downside to 1381 is -3%" as if 2x ATR is a contractual guarantee. But you're computing that stop off an ATR that the technical report shows is *re-expanding* — 21.22 on 6/11 back up to 22.70 on 6/13 — in a stock that just broke the 200-day, broke the Bollinger lower band, and has a MACD histogram re-widening at -10.71. Scaling a stop off a volatility measure that is itself accelerating is circular. Worse, the technical report literally tells you what's below: 1425 is the immediate support, and beneath it the report calls the zone a 真空地带 — no近端支撑 until 1400 psychological, then 1380-1385. With T+1, a gap through 1400 means your "defined -3%" fills somewhere you didn't choose. That's not a defined-risk trade, that's a hope dressed in a number. And your "capitulation volume" read — 591万股 at 2.8x — is a plausible interpretation, but the sentiment report is explicit that it's still "放量下行途中," not "缩量止跌." You're inferring the last shakeout from volume *expansion*, which is precisely the pattern that can extend for another week before it exhausts. You may be right about direction; you're wrong to call it defined risk.

But Conservative, you're overcorrecting in the opposite direction, and your strongest point is actually weaker than you present it. Yes, T+1 and limit-down traps are real structural constraints — I take that seriously and it should shape sizing. But you're using "we might not be able to sell tomorrow" as a blanket veto on *any* risk-taking, and that's not what the constraint actually implies. The T+1 framework doesn't say "never hold through an overnight"; it says "size positions so that a single overnight gap-down is survivable." Those are different conclusions. Your framing treats the gap risk as binary — either we're flat or we're trapped — when the actual solution the framework prescribes is a moderate position that can absorb a gap and still leave optionality. You've also quietly inflated the gap risk: a limit-down on a 16,000亿 market cap with 2000亿 in cash-like assets and a state controlling shareholder is not the same probability event as a limit-down on a small-cap题材股. The technical report's own note is that 6/13's -2.19% was *nowhere near* the ±10% limit and liquidity was normal. You're pricing a tail as if it's the base case.

And your "we give up 8-10% but we buy at 1520-1550 with confirmation" argument has a hidden cost you're not counting. If the 7-8月中报 shows contract liabilities holding at 87.88亿 or growing, and the stock re-rates from 20x toward the 25x band, you're not buying at 1520-1550 — you're buying after a 15-20% move, and the risk-reward at that point is *worse* than it is now because you've paid for the confirmation. The conservative framework's "survive first" logic is correct, but "survive" doesn't mean "only enter after the move." It means "size so that being early doesn't kill you."

So here's where I land, and it's genuinely between you two. The neutral framework's core insight — that position sizing dominates directional conviction in a ±10% / T+1 market — is the right organizing principle, and neither of you is fully honoring it. Aggressive wants to treat this as a conviction long with a tight stop; Conservative wants to treat it as un-enterable until confirmation. The framework says: hold the existing exposure you already have (which the trader's decision correctly does), and if you want to *add*, add in a tranche small enough that a gap through 1400 to 1385 is annoying but not portfolio-damaging — not the full aggressive sizing, and not zero. That's the position-sized middle: you capture the mean-reversion edge Aggressive is right about *if* it materializes, while the size respects Conservative's correct point that the stop isn't executable in a gap.

On the specific debate points: Aggressive is right that the policy report grades the net effect "中性偏利好（结构性）" with a real floor, and Conservative is right that a floor caps downside without paying you to buy a broken chart — both true, and they net out to "policy supports holding, not a reason to add aggressively." Aggressive is right that the 2.8x volume dump with zero news catalyst is positioning-driven, and positioning-driven selloffs reverse on positioning — but Conservative is right that "positioning-driven" doesn't tell you *when*, and the sentiment report says the reversal signals (缩量止跌, RSI-MACD底背离, reclaim 1485) are all absent. That's exactly why you size, not why you either slam in or stand aside.

One thing neither of you handled well: the valuation. Aggressive, you cited PE 20x against a 25-35x band as if it's a discount — but the fundamentals report explicitly flags that PE snapshot as a future-dated function, not the 2025-06-13 value, so you're anchoring on a number of uncertain provenance. Conservative, you correctly caught that but then used the uncertainty to justify doing nothing, when the honest read is "we don't have a clean valuation anchor, so don't let valuation be the load-bearing beam of either the bull or bear case." The load-bearing beam should be the supply-side facts (fully floated, zero unlocks, no controlling-shareholder selling history — all verified) plus the fundamental floor (91.97% gross margin, 40% ROE, 14% debt — all verified), and the honest admission that the *timing* catalyst is the 7-8月中报, which is unknown. That combination argues for holding existing exposure and, at most, a modest tranche add near 1425-1431 with sizing that survives a gap to 1385 — not the aggressive full-size conviction trade, and not the conservative refusal to act.

So I'm endorsing HOLD, but with a sharper rationale than the trader's "wait for three confirmations": hold because the verified facts (clean float, elite fundamentals, policy floor) say don't sell into a positioning-driven flush, and the unverified facts (中报 contract liabilities, 批价, the actual current PE) say don't size up as if the re-rating is confirmed. If you want to express the Aggressive view, do it as a *small* tranche where a gap-down through 1400 is survivable — that's the T+1 framework's actual prescription, not a veto and not a conviction bet. The Conservative analyst is right that the burden of proof for adding risk sits on the buyer; the Aggressive analyst is right that the burden is met by the supply-side and fundamental facts, just not by enough to justify full sizing before the tape confirms. Position sizing is the answer both of you keep skipping past — and it's the only answer that respects a market where your stop executes at the gap, not at 1381.
